title: Undo for an editor with opaque snapshots

task.text: Give the editor undo without letting anyone outside it read or forge its state.

items: `Editor.save()` returns a **memento** of the text and cursor; `Editor.restore(m)` returns the editor to it. Replace the `Object` placeholders with a dedicated type that code outside `Editor` can neither read nor construct.
A snapshot is immutable and unaffected by later edits. Restoring one twice gives the same result.
`History(Editor)` is the caretaker: `checkpoint()` stores the current snapshot, `undo()` restores the latest one and returns `true`, or returns `false` when none is left.
`History` never looks inside a snapshot or reads the editor's state.

checks.title: Restore brings back text and cursor
Later edits do not change a snapshot
Undo with no checkpoint returns false
Checkpoints still work after an undo
save() returns a dedicated memento type
Outside Editor, a memento cannot be read or forged
History only stores and hands back mementos

hints.text: Only the originator understands its own state, so only it should create and open snapshots. The caretaker stores them blindly. Copy mutable state; never share the `StringBuilder`.
Declare a nested `Memento` type with no readable members, backed by a private immutable record inside `Editor`. `History` keeps a `Deque` of them and calls only `save` and `restore`.

lines: private record Snapshot(String text, int cursor) implements Memento { }
Memento save() { return new Snapshot(text.toString(), cursor); }
